subject: ordering of scale colours to match order of bars in histogram

messages.author: e7e95b47f1608404
messages.subject: ordering of scale colours to match order of bars in histogram
parts:
Dear all,
For the histograms (geom_bar filled with a categorical variable) the
colour legend is ranked in the opposite order of the histogram, making
the reading of the chart a bit complicated (see for example the right
hand side of figures 4.6 and 2.12 of Hadley's book - 24 February
version). Could they not be ordered in the same way?
Kind regards,
Ivan

messages.author: e7e95b47f1608404
messages.subject: Re: ordering of scale colours to match order of bars in histogram
parts:
I am using version 0.8.2.  The examples of the book are pretty clear (see the code for Figure 2.12 below).  The issue is not one of ordering of the factors, but rather of the matching between the stacks in the plot (from top to down) and those of the legend (also from top to down).  ggplot stacks the histogram starting from the bottom (in the order of the factors) and the legends stacks them from the top (also in the order of the factors), resulting in an "inverse ordering" of stacks.

qplot(carat, data = diamonds, geom = "histogram", fill = color)

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: ordering of scale colours to match order of bars in histogram
parts:
Hi Bob,

You can work around this by manually specifying the ordering of the
breaks in the legend:

+ scale_colour_hue(breaks = rev(levels(diamonds$color)))

I did used to have the legends in the opposite order to alleviate just
this problem, but it hurts in more cases than it helps.

Hadley
